flow.netIncomeNote: The bottom line: $1,295M kept as profit, 29.1% of revenue.
flow.operatingIncomeNote: A $1,563M operating profit — 35.1% of revenue, up from $1,248M a year ago.

opex.note: Designing new analog and embedded chips; up from $498M a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; up from $465M a year ago.

flow.revenueNote: Money from selling analog and embedded processing chips.
flow.taxNote: A $183M tax provision on $1,478M of pre-tax income — a 12.4% effective rate, helped by a $16M discrete tax benefit.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to the nearest cent, so the rounded rows sum to the rounded $29.11 of profit per $100.
oneTimers: A $16M discrete tax benefit (about 2 cents of EPS) that was not in the company's original guidance — operating taxes were $199M, less $16M of discrete items, for a $183M provision.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net of $48M, less $133M of interest and debt expense — a net $85M drag. The $183M tax provision is $199M of operating taxes less a $16M discrete tax benefit.

segments.name: Analog
segments.note: Analog chips — the workhorse of industrial and automotive electronics; up 18% YoY. Segment operating profit was $1,325M.

segments.name: Embedded Processing
segments.note: Microcontrollers and processors for connected devices; up 10% YoY. Segment operating profit was $85M.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Smaller product lines, including DLP and calculators; up 14% YoY. Segment operating profit was $153M.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Jun 30, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 16% to $4.45B and 9% sequentially, led by a continued broad recovery in industrial demand. Analog, the biggest business, grew 18% to $3.45B; Embedded Processing grew 10% and Other grew 14% — growth across every segment.
takeaways.title: The industrial recovery showed up in every segment

takeaways.text: Operating profit rose 25% to $1.56B, a 35.1% operating margin, on gross profit of $2.58B. R&D and SG&A together were $1.01B, up just 5% while revenue grew 16% — the extra sales fell mostly to the bottom line. Net income rose 15% to $1.30B and EPS rose 16% to $1.41.
takeaways.title: Sales grew three times faster than spending

takeaways.text: Over the past 12 months TI returned $6.71B to owners — $4.90B in dividends and $1.81B in buybacks — while investing $4.94B in new factories. Free cash flow for the same period was $1.76B, just 10.6% of revenue, because that factory spending is so heavy. Q3 guidance is $4.45–$4.80B of revenue and EPS of $1.36–$1.60.
takeaways.title: Big payouts, bigger factory bill

verdict: Texas Instruments earned $1.30 billion on $4.45 billion of revenue as sales grew 16% on a broad recovery in industrial demand, with operating profit up 25%.
